Quamrul Islam Siddique J: This is an application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for enlarging the accused petitioner on anticipatory bail in Motijheel Police Station Case No.6 dated 4-1-2015 under sections 186/307/427/436/109 of the Penal Code read with sections 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, now pending in the court of learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 3. The prosecution case in short is that on 4-1-2015 at 13-45 hours, the accused petitioner along with 80 FIR named accused conspired and blasted bombs and torched the vehicle, namely, Dhaka Metro Ga-37-9347 Toyota. The vehicle was burnt into ashes and there was a loss of Taka 35,00,000. The accused-petitioner torched the vehicle by blasting bombs and thereby committed an offence under sections 186/ 307/ 427/ 436/ 109 of the Penal Code read with sections 3/6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908. The informant then lodged the FIR with Motijheel Police Station. 

 (1) State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury, 51 DLR (AD) 242, 

 (2) Durnity Daman Commission vs Dr Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, 66 DLR (AD) 92, 

 (1) State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury, 51 DLR (AD) 242;7 

 (2) Durnity Daman Commission vs Dr Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, 66 DLR (AD) 92; 

 17. During hearing, a question arose whether this Court is competent to grant anticipatory bail to the accused-petitioner in view of the decisions. reported in 51 DLR (AD) 242, 66 DLR (AD) 92, 31 BLD (AD) 20 and 3 CLR (AD) 11. 

 1. State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury published in 51 DLR (AD) 242 

 19. In the case of State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury published in 51 DLR (AD) 242, in paragraph 20, it has been stated as under: 

 23. Admittedly in the case in hand, charge-sheet has not been submitted by the police as yet. So, from the decision published in 51 DLR (AD) 242, there is no difficulty on the part of the High Court Division to grant an accused anticipatory bail if extraordinary and exceptional circumstances exist. Again, it is the Court to decide whether such exceptional and extraordinary circumstances exist for getting anticipatory bail. 

 2. Durnity Daman Commission vs Dr Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain 66 DLR (AD) 92 

 24. Now, let us discuss the second case, that is, the case of Durnity Daman Commission vs Dr Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, 66 DLR (AD) 92. In this case, it has been held in para 24(f) as under: 

 "24. (f) The High Court Division must scrutinize the text in the FIR with expected diligence and shall ordinarily be indisposed to grant anticipatory bail where the allegations are of heinous nature, keeping in mind the ordains figured at paragraph 19 of the case reported in 51 DLR (AD), supra. Claim that the allegations are cooked up shall also not be adjudged at that point if the FIR or the complaint petition, as the case is prima facie, discloses an offence. Whether the allegations are framed or genuine can only be determined through investigation and sifting of evidence." 

 "14. This Division in different cases particularly, in cases of State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury, 51 DLR (AD) 243 and State vs Zakaria Pintu reported in 31 BLD (AD) 20 has given specific indications regarding scope and authority of exercising such extraordinary judicial discretion of the High Court Division. Such discretion has to be exercised with due care and circumspection depending on circumstances justifying its exercise. No blanket order of bail should be passed. Such power of the High Court Division is not unguided or uncontrolled and should be exercised in exceptional cases only." 

 51. On 4-1-2015 at about 10-30 pm, Suman Chandra Nath, Sub-Inspector of Police, Motijheel Police Station, Dhaka Metropolitan Police lodged a First Information Report (FIR) with the same Police Station against the accused-petitioner and 80 other FIR-named accused-persons along with 20-30 unknown accused-persons, who belong to the 20-Party Alliance. The FIR was registered as Motijheel Police Station Case No.6 dated 4-1- 2015 under sections 186/307/427/436/109 of the Penal Code read with sections 3 and 6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908, now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. It was alleged in the FIR that on 4-1-2015, while the informant along with his companion forces was on mobile duty namely Kilo-l Mobile Duty, the driver of a Toyota Primio Private Car bearing Registration No. Dhaka Metro Ga-37- 9347, having dropped Major Rashed off in front of the Baitul Mamur Jame Mosque, AGB Coloney, Motijheel, was waiting there with the car. At about 1-25 pm, even before he could guess anything, all of a sudden, in an intention to deteriorate the law and order situation by creating terror and panic, and perpetrating subversive activities for making a success of the 'hartal' called to be observed on 5-1-2015, the unknown leaders and activists of the 20-Party Alliance under the leadership, and at the order and the instigation of the absconding accused-persons, including the accused-petitioner set the car ablaze with combustible substances. In an ill intention to kill the driver of the car, the unknown accused-persons also hurled two bombs at the car which made the area covered with smokes and caused the passersby to run hither and thither in panic. The accused- persons by burning the car to ashes caused damage of Taka-35 lakh. Accordingly, the informant filed the case. The case is still under investigation. In the facts and circumstances, the petitioner on surrender before this Court filed the instant application for anticipatory bail in the case. 

 54. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate having adopted the submission of Mr. Khandker Mahbub Hossain and also having relied upon the decisions made in the case of State vs Abdul Wahab Shah. Chowdhury, 51 DLR (AD) 242, particularly paragraph Nos. 21 and 23 thereof submits that the criminal proceeding which is being or has been launched against the accused-petitioner is being or has been taken with an ulterior motive, political or otherwise, for harassing the accused-petitioner and not for securing justice and thus, the purpose of filing of the case against the accused-petitioner is not what it purports to be, but to achieve a collateral purpose by abusing the process of law and, as such, the petitioner may be granted anticipatory bail. 

 60. With regard to the principles on granting anticipatory bail, in paragraph No. 23 of the case of State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury, 51 DLR (AD) 242, the Appellate Division laid down as below- 

 61. The Appellate Division endorsed the above view almost in every subsequent cases, including the cases of the State vs Zakaria Pintu alias Md Zakaria Pintu, 62 DLR (AD) 420, Durnity Daman Commission vs Dr Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, 66 DLR (AD) 92 and the State vs Mirza Abbas, 3 CLR (AD) 11. 

 63. It appears from the FIR that it was filed on 4-1-2015, but the election schedule has been declared very recently. Therefore, the case had been filed long before the election schedule was declared. Moreover, the FIR does not disclose that the filing of the case had any nexus with the ensuing election of Dhaka South City Corporation. Nevertheless, the case was lodged against several senior leaders of Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) including its Secretary General and the petitioner. Some of the accused are also the senior leaders of Jamat-E-Islami and other component political parties of the 20-Party Alliance. So, it cannot be said that all 81 FIR named accused-persons were prospective candidates from the same Alliance for the same post of Mayor of Dhaka South City Corporation. Thus, the petitioner has failed to make out any case as to that the case in hand was filed with an ulterior motive so that he would not be able to contest the ensuing election of Dhaka South City Corporation freely and without any hindrance. Nevertheless, in similar context, in the case of Durnity Daman Commission vs Dr Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, 66 DLR (AD) . 92, the Appellate Division held as under: 

 65. Moreover, it appears that the Hartal was to be observed on 5-1-2015, but the occurrence took place on 4-1-2015, just before the day the Hartal was to be observed and it has been alleged in the FIR that under the leadership, and at the order and the instigation of the petitioner and other absconding accused-persons, the perpetrators committed the serious offences. In this regard the case of the State vs Mirza Abbas, reported in 3 CLR (AD) 11 may be referred to further. In all four cases as were involved therein, the similar allegation of abetment of offence i.e. the respondents (the present petitioner and others) named in the body of the FIR planned, conspired and financed the miscreants to commit such offence and in those cases, the Appellate Division did not approve the orders of the High Court Division granting anticipatory bail to the present petitioner. In this regard, having referred to different cases, particularly, the case of State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury, 51 DLR (AD) 242 and State vs Zakaria Pintu alias Md Zakaria Pintu and others, 31 BLD (AD) 20 corresponding to 62 DLR (AD) 420, the Appellate Division held therein as below- 

 66. Since similar, allegations of abetment of offence has also been brought against the accused-petitioner in the case in hand, it would be, to say the least, a judicial indiscipline to grant the accused-petitioner anticipatory bail in the given facts of the case. Nonetheless, in a series of decisions, both Divisions of this Court respectively held that a judgment passed by the High Court Division contrary to the judgment of the Appellate Division or a judgment passed by the subordinate Court contrary to the judgment passed by either Division of this Court is perverse and illegal, and may be contemptuous. In this regard the case of Nurjahan Begum vs AFM Abdullah, reported in 13 BLC 535, Amzad Hossain vs State, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 288 and State vs Mukta Khan, reported in 2011 BLD (AD) 110 may be referred to. 

 67. The conduct of the accused-petitioner and others as has been projected in the FIR ignited violence over and against the common people in the vicinity. The Appellate Division in the case of State vs Zakaria Pintu alias Md Zakaria Pintu, 62 DLR (AD) 420 made it imperative on the part of the Court to refuse the accused anticipatory bail if there is serious allegation against him, like murder, rape, violence etc. In that case the Appellate Division held as under- 

 68. Another aspect of the case is that the case was filed on 4-1-2015 and the petitioner appeared before this Court only on 13-4-2015 with this application. It appears from the case of the State vs Zakaria hntu alias Md Md Zakaria Pintu, reported in 62 DLR (AD) 420 that the occurrence involved therein took place on 27-11-2009 and the High Court Division granted the petitioner there- in anticipatory bail on 8-12-2009 i.e. only after 11 days of the filing of case, but the Appellate Division in the paragraph No. 14 of the decision held as under: 

 70. Anticipatory bail cannot be granted on mere request of an accused, however high his position may be in the society, unless he can satisfy other conditions for such bail. In this regard, the caution spelt out by Justice SA Rahman in the case of Sadiq Ali vs State, 18 DLR (SC) 393 should be borne in mind in disposing of any application for anticipatory bail, which runs as follows:- 

 71. In the case of State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury, 51 DLR (AD) 242, the Appellate Division also reminded the above caution in the following terms- 

 75. In the light of the decision made in the case of the State vs Zakaria Pintu alias Md Zakaria Pintu, 62 DLR (AD) 420, it has already been found that such a petitioner who comes at a belated stage for anticipatory bail is deemed to be a fugitive and in this regard the Appellate Division held therein as under- 

 Md Ruhul Quddus J: This application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is filed for anticipatory bail of the petitioner Mirza Abbas Uddin Ahmed, a former Minister, central leader of Bangladesh Nationalist Party (in brief BNP) and candidate in the immediately past Mayoral election of Dhaka City Corporation in Motijheel Police Station Case No. 6 dated 4-1- 2015 under sections 186, 307, 427, 436 and 109 of the Penal Code read with sections 3 and 6 of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908 now pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 82. Mr Mohammad Ali further submits that actually the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the case to keep him out from the mayoral race. He refers to the text of the ejahar and further submits that, admittedly the persons allegedly set the vehicle on fire were unknown to the informant and there is no allegation of overt act against the petitioner. In such a case where no offender could be identified by the informant, how the petitioner can be referred to as a leader and instructor without any specific information to that effect. The political and social image, status and position of the petitioner indicate that the allegations brought against him are absurd. In the present case anticipatory bail can also be granted to the petitioner for his protection from hostile attitude of the government agencies. In support of his contention Mr Mohammad Ali refers to the case of State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury, 51 DLR (AD) 242 and Golam Sarwar Kamal vs State, 5 BLD (AD) 110. 

 84. Learned Attorney-General further submits that the present case is brought for commission of heinous offences like explosions of bombs, setting a car on fire and attempting to kill its driver. In such a case only because of infirmity, if any, in the ejahar lodged, an accused prominently named therein however high his position and status is cannot be granted anticipatory bail. A brief reflection on the facts and circumstances of the case and the prevailing situation of the Country is enough to draw an inference that the petitioner was involved in the alleged occurrence, and all other occurrences that took place in the recent past. Mr Attorney-General further submits that in some other cases of similar nature anticipatory bail granted to the same petitioner has been disapproved by the Appellate Division. He then refers to the case of State vs Mirza Abbas, 3 CLR (AD), 11 and also refers the cases of State vs Zakaria Pintu alias Md Zakaria Pintu, 62 DLR(AD) 420 =31 BLD (AD) 20; Durnity Daman Commission vs Dr Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, 66 DLR (AD) 92 in support of his submissions. 

 85. Let me consider first whether an application for anticipatory bail can be rejected for default in case of failure of the petitioner to appear in person before the third judge, while sitting on a dissenting judgment referred to him by the Hon'ble Chief Justice for disposal. In a similar case [Belayet Hossain Sharif (Md) vs State, 50 DLR 242] the point whether the third judge without deciding an application for anticipatory bail on merit could reject, it as not being pressed was considered. In that case allegation of cheating and misappropriation of some pledged, vegetable oil was brought by a creditor bank against an eminent Industrialist. He moved an application for anticipatory bail before this Division, upon which the presiding judge Mr Justice Muhammad Abdul Mannan granted anticipatory bail till submission of police report and disposed of the application, while Mr Justice Syed Amirul Islam sitting with him rejected the same summarily. Accordingly the matter was referred to the third judge. When it was taken up for hearing, the learned Advocate for the petitioner at the outset made a prayer for rejecting the application as not being pressed apprising that in the meantime the petitioner had surrendered before the Court below and already obtained bail, and, as such, the application itself became infructuous. 

 93. I have also gone through the decisions cited and some other decisions on this subject. In the case of State vs Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury, 51 DLR (AD) 242 two criminal appeals were heard and disposed of together. In the first one, the respondent was accused allegedly for abduction and killing of victim Shahidul Islam, nephew of the informant. The informant was not an eyewitness to the occurrence, but came to learn it from others and some earlier incidents that then respondent had secretly advised to commit the offence. In moving the application for anticipatory bail before the High Court Division the respondent stated that he was an old man of 76 years age and unable to move without assistance of others. He was a leader of BNP haying political rivalry with the informant, for which he was falsely implicated in the case. It was also alleged that the Magistrates were under control of the ruling party and, as such, his case for bail would not be dealt with justly and judicially. In the second one, the petitioner before the High Court Division was an accused in a girl abduction case. In both the cases the High Court Division granted anticipatory bail to the accused-petitioners, challenging which the State went up to the Appellate Division. The Appellate Division granted leave and ultimately allowed the appeals deciding some principles of granting anticipatory bail. 

 96. On the other hand, in series of subsequent cases the Appellate Division though affirmed the ratio of Abdul Wahab Shah Chowdhury's case, has interpreted the law relating to anticipatory bail more, strictly. In the case of State vs Zakaria Pintu alias Md Zakaria Pintu, 62 DLR (AD) 420 = 31 BLD (AD) 20 some accused in a murder case pending before the concerned Chief Judicial Magistrate had moved in this Division with an application for anticipatory bail, wherein Rule was issued and petitioner 1 was granted anticipatory bail for a period of six months or till submission of police report whichever was earlier, and the application was disposed of so far it was related to other petitioners with a direction upon them to surrender before the concerned Sessions Judge. The High Court Division further directed the police not to arrest them in the meantime and also directed the Sessions Judge to consider their prayer for bail, if any. The State being aggrieved therewith moved in the Appellate Division with a criminal petition for leave to appeal. The Appellate Division initially stayed the impugned order of the High Court and on hearing of the leave petition disposed of the same with observation of disapproval and continued with the stay order till disposal of the miscellaneous case by the High Court Division. In the said judgment ABM, Khairul Haque, J (as his lordship then was) speaking for the Court cautioned/reminded all concerned in the following, words:
